---
title: "How to Contribute"
---

The MISP User Guide grows through the experience of the people who use, operate, teach, and develop MISP.
You do not need to write code or be a MISP expert to help.
A corrected sentence, a reproducible report of a confusing step, or a review of a procedure can make the next reader's work easier.

The book's source is maintained in [MISP/misp-book](https://github.com/MISP/misp-book).
Use its [issues](https://github.com/MISP/misp-book/issues) to report documentation problems or propose work, and its [pull requests](https://github.com/MISP/misp-book/pulls) to submit changes for review.
For a substantial new chapter or reorganization, discuss the scope in an issue before investing in the full change.

## Choose a way to help {#contribution-options}

- **Report an error or missing explanation.** Identify the page and the point where the instructions stop being useful; a proposed fix is welcome but not required.
- **Improve the writing.** Correct spelling, explain a term, simplify an ambiguous instruction, improve a caption, or connect a page to the relevant [glossary](../glossary.qmd) entry.
- **Test a procedure.** Follow it on a known MISP version and report the result, prerequisites, required role, and any missing steps.
- **Share a use case.** Describe a question, the observations available, the investigation steps, the result, and the limitations so another reader can repeat the method.
- **Update illustrations.** Replace an outdated screenshot or improve a diagram's labels, structure, accessibility, or explanation.
- **Review a proposed change.** Check technical accuracy, readability, examples, links, and whether the instructions work for the intended audience.
- **Help with language and translations.** Improve the English text or discuss a translation with maintainers so the source, destination, and update process are clear.

## Report a documentation problem {#contribution-issues}

Search the [open issues](https://github.com/MISP/misp-book/issues) first; an existing report may already describe the problem.
If it does, add any new reproduction details there.
Otherwise, [open an issue](https://github.com/MISP/misp-book/issues/new) with a title that identifies the affected page and problem.

Include the page URL and section heading, what you expected to understand or achieve, what the text currently says, and a suggested correction if you have one.
For a procedure or screenshot, state the MISP version or branch, your user role, relevant prerequisites, and the steps you followed.
For a layout problem, identify HTML, PDF, or ePub and the browser or reader involved.
Use sanitized examples that can be shared publicly; omit credentials, session cookies, private threat intelligence, and personal information.

Report defects in the MISP application to the [MISP core issue tracker](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/issues), and component-specific problems to that component's repository.
Link the related report when the book also needs a correction.

## Make a small edit in your browser {#contribution-browser}

You can propose a text change without installing Git, Quarto, or MISP:

1. Open the relevant page in the online book and select **Edit this page**, or find its source file in the repository.
2. Sign in to GitHub and use its file editor. If you do not have write access, GitHub will guide you through creating a fork.
3. Edit the `.qmd` source, which is Markdown with a short metadata header. Preserve the surrounding structure and existing heading identifiers.
4. Commit the change to a branch in your fork and open a pull request against **MISP/misp-book**, base branch **main**.
5. Explain the reader's problem, what changed, and how you checked it. Link the relevant issue, then respond to review comments and check results.

For a broken link or typo, a short explanation is enough.
For changed procedures, describe the version tested and the observed result so reviewers can assess the claim.

## Work on a larger change locally {#contribution-local}

Fork the repository on GitHub, then clone your fork and create a focused branch.
Replace `YOUR-ACCOUNT` with your GitHub account:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/YOUR-ACCOUNT/misp-book.git
cd misp-book
git switch -c docs/improve-a-procedure
```

Most chapters are stored as `<chapter>/index.qmd`; illustrations belong in that chapter's `figures/` directory.
The root `_quarto.yml` defines the reading order and output formats.
When adding a chapter, register it in the appropriate part and add useful links from related pages.

Install [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/), using the version pinned in the repository's [build workflow](https://github.com/MISP/misp-book/blob/main/.github/workflows/quarto.yml) for reproducible results.
Preview while editing, then render the book:

```sh
quarto preview
```

Stop the preview with Ctrl+C before running the full checks:

```sh
quarto render
quarto render --profile pdf-smoke --to typst
```

The main render produces HTML, PDF, and ePub in `_book/`.
The smoke profile checks representative PDF cross-reference layouts.
Inspect the changed pages in the relevant formats, including a narrow browser window for new tables or figures.
Ordinary documentation builds reuse committed `_freeze/` results and do not require a live MISP instance or API key.
If you intentionally update executable examples, follow the [README's refresh procedure](https://github.com/MISP/misp-book/blob/main/README.md#executable-code-chapters) and review the frozen output before committing it.

Commit the source changes, push your branch to your fork, and open a pull request against `main`.
Generated `_book/` and `_book-pdf-smoke/` output should remain outside the commit.
GitHub Actions renders the formats, checks the PDF smoke profile, and validates internal links and anchors; investigate any failed check and describe unresolved issues in the PR.
Passing automated checks supports review but does not replace checking the procedure itself.
Maintainers review and merge accepted changes.

## Add useful examples, screenshots, and diagrams {#contribution-illustrations}

Describe the version or source revision you tested, the role used, and any configuration needed to reproduce a procedure.
Distinguish current behavior from a proposed feature or an observation from an older branch.
Link to maintained installation instructions and component documentation rather than copying long procedures that can drift independently.

Capture screenshots from the interface you describe, using a dedicated test instance and shareable data.
Prefer reserved domains and addresses for constructed examples and label them as synthetic.
Show the relevant controls at a readable size, add meaningful alternative text and a caption, and state the version captured.
Keep credentials and private records out of the capture.
Record provenance alongside version-specific illustrations, following the existing chapter manifests in `assets/`.

For Mermaid diagrams, edit the `.mmd` source beside the figure and use the shared renderer to generate its SVG.
The [diagram guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-book/blob/main/assets/diagrams/README.md) explains the MISP theme, automatic logo, accessible labels, dependencies, and regeneration command.
Commit the source, generated SVG, and updated diagram manifest together.
For generated category/type tables, follow the [data model reference guide](https://github.com/MISP/misp-book/blob/main/assets/data-model/README.md) instead of editing generated rows by hand.

## Review, language, and related MISP contributions {#contribution-review}

Reviewers can help by following the proposed instructions, checking whether a different role sees the same controls, or identifying an unsupported conclusion.
Leave feedback that names the affected passage, explains the problem, and suggests a clearer alternative where possible.
Report what you tested rather than implying coverage of versions or environments you did not use.

The book uses American English and English interface examples.
Language corrections are welcome from all contributors.
For a book translation, open an issue to agree on the language, publication format, and how it will track source updates; translating the application interface is a separate activity covered in [MISP and Internationalization](../translation/index.qmd).

Changes to MISP code, object templates, taxonomies, galaxies, warninglists, or modules belong in their own repositories and follow those projects' contribution instructions.
The book can explain the resulting behavior and link to it; see [MISP Objects](../misp-objects/index.qmd), [Taxonomies](../taxonomy/index.qmd), [Galaxies](../galaxy/index.qmd), [Warninglists](../warninglists/index.qmd), and [MISP Modules](../modules/index.qmd) for the relevant context.

## Style, attribution, and community {#contribution-credit}

Use clear headings, relative `.qmd` links within the book, fenced code blocks with a language, and one sentence per source line where practical.
Preserve existing anchors when changing headings, and explain acronyms before relying on them.
The repository's [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/MISP/misp-book/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) summarize the source conventions.

The guide is dual-licensed under [AGPLv3](https://www.gnu.org/licenses/agpl-3.0.html) and [CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/).
Check that material you contribute can be shared under the applicable terms, credit external sources, and retain any material-specific notices and licenses.
Treat other participants respectfully and follow the MISP project's [code of conduct](https://github.com/MISP/MISP/blob/3.0_wip/code_of_conduct.md).
The [Acknowledgements](../acknowledgements/index.qmd) recognize the community behind this guide.
